notes: The deployed RPC deduplicates destination thread IDs, authorizes every destination before its first write and propagates insert or attachment failures so PostgreSQL rolls back the whole RPC.

The real release probe mixed one authorized and one unauthorized destination and observed partialCopyDelta 0. The duplicate-destination probe created one provisional copy and persistentCopyDelta returned to 0 after rollback to its savepoint.

The successful mutation report is bound to 86c395be. The later Product SHA changes only failure-outcome reconciliation, contract assertions and SQL end-of-file whitespace; the exact-head read-only deployment report proves that the atomic definition and migration ledger remain installed.

A full AES-256-GCM logical backup was created through TLS verify-full with its key stored separately and no plaintext dump retained. A full restore drill succeeded in an isolated Supabase PostgreSQL 17.6.1.143 database and verified the required Chat function and tables.

Three earlier release attempts failed before commit because the direct session lacked authenticated JWT context. Each transaction rolled back and a read-only probe confirmed the historic function and absent ledger before the corrected release; failed reports remain local and are not acceptance evidence.

No artificial failure was injected after the first destination insert. The later-write rollback guarantee is established by the reviewed SQL structure: there is no per-destination exception handler and PostgreSQL executes the function call as one statement.

No platform E2E matrix was repeated because Android, Web/Wasm and iOS client runtime code did not change; all clients already use the shared RPC and their existing picker, failure and retry evidence remains applicable.
No connection string, credential, profile ID, thread ID, message ID, backup key or absolute private path is present in the committed reports.
